transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kaur (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Redwood CSM), Maria Gonzalez (NexaHead of ML), Tom Ryder (Platform Eng), Samantha Lee (Security), Evan Brooks (Data Scientist)

Summary (auto):
- Reviewed week-over-week benchmarks comparing v0.9 (quantized) vs v1.0 (full precision) and a fallback smaller family (m-lite-3B).
- Discussed pinning v0.9 to production canary with automated rollback to v1.0 if quality regressions detected, and fallback to m-lite on capacity or cost triggers.
- Agreed on next steps: share raw CSVs, run expanded eval, create rollback runbook, confirm compliance docs.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Alex: ok hey everyone thanks for joining the POC weekly, um let's do quick intros then jump into the bench results.
[00:08] Maria: hi Maria here, head of ML at Nexa, thanks.
[00:12] Tom: Tom, platform. we have the infra notes ready.
[00:16] Samantha: Samantha from security.
[00:19] Evan: Evan, running the evals.
[00:22] Priya: Priya from Redwood, SE on the account.
[00:25] Daniel: Daniel, CSM.
[00:27] Alex: cool. quick agenda, bench recap, pinning proposal, rollback/fallback options, action items. Sound good?
[00:34] Group: yes / yep.

[00:45] Evan: so we ran the 1k and then expanded to 1.5k prompts last night. results - latency median for v0.9 quantized was 82 ms per token on average under our sample; v1.0 full precision was 120 ms, and m-lite-3B was 60 ms but quality lower on medical QA prompts.
[01:05] Maria: uh can you repeat the 82? was that p99 or median?
[01:09] Evan: median sorry, p95 was 230 ms for v0.9, v1.0 p95 is 380 ms. so quantization helped burst latency but p95 still sometimes spikey.
[01:22] Priya: yeah that's consistent with what we saw — quantized runtime picks better kernels and smaller memory paths, but sequence length distributions from Nexa's prompts push the cache thrashing. sometimes KV cache gets reset more often... or as the transcript says the KV "cash" uh cache.
[01:38] Tom: we noticed a couple spikes when patients' notes were long, like >3k tokens. is there a recommended approach?
[01:45] Priya: two immediate levers: prefix trimming + dynamic chunking at the client, and pinning a model variant with larger context kernel, or using the dedicated slot with higher memory. both have cost tradeoffs.
[02:00] Maria: tradeoffs, yes. our success criteria is sub-250ms median and <400ms p95 for interactive flows, and hallucination rate under 3% on the eval set.
[02:12] Alex: good to have numbers. on pinning — we propose to pin v0.9 quantized as the canary for 10% of traffic, keep v1.0 available as immediate rollback and m-lite-3B as cost-efficient fallback when cost thresholds hit.
[02:28] Samantha: from security perspective we need to confirm that the quantized artifacts still pass our reproducibility checks and that KMS keys are used for model artifacts in private. also audit logs.
[02:40] Alex: yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated both support KMS/HSM for keys and the control plane records model versioning events in audit logs. we'll share the SOC2 and evidence links.
[02:52] Samantha: great, please share link.

[03:05] Evan: on quality, v0.9 showed a slight uptick in hallucinations on the 'rare diseases' subset — about 4.2% vs 2.8% on v1.0, so above our 3% threshold. but when we applied the prompt engineering changes suggested last week (explicit citation anchor and guardrails) the rate dropped to 2.9% for v0.9.
[03:27] Maria: oh that's interesting — so mix of model + prompt tuning might get us under threshold. can we replicate that across the 2k set?
[03:35] Evan: yes i'm scheduling that run, should finish by Friday. it's in next steps.

[03:45] Priya: the pinning strategy can also use automatic quality gates — Redwood supports regression checks on per-prompt cohorts. We can set the gate: if hallucination delta > 0.5% or BLEU/ROUGE drops by X, auto rollback to v1.0. the gating runs on a shadow sampling set for the canary.
[04:07] Alex: to clarify, the rollback is immediate traffic switch to v1.0, and fallback to m-lite is a separate policy triggered by cost per token > threshold or Dedicated capacity pressure.
[04:18] Tom: how fast is rollback? seconds, minutes?
[04:21] Priya: rollbacks are near-instant at the routing layer — we aim for <30s for the traffic flip, but onboard tests and warmup may add a couple minutes to reach steady-state.
[04:33] Maria: what about session continuity? if a user is mid-session and we flip model versions will we lose context?
[04:39] Priya: good question. for chat sessions we persist the KV cache keyed to model+session id. if model family differs (e.g., m-lite-3B) KV compatibility may not hold, so we recommend a fallback that restarts the session or uses a retry with a graceful degradation message. will document in runbook.

[05:00] Samantha: also logging - we need per-token cost attribution and encryption of logs at rest; do you support field-level redaction?
[05:08] Alex: yes Redwood Console supports token-level cost/latency breakdown. field-level PII redaction is available via pre-ingest hooks or you can send us a redaction spec and we can pattern-match before retention. logs are encrypted and stored per customer.
[05:23] Samantha: ok please send the compliance artifact link.

[05:45] Evan: quick note on benchmarks — we saw an anomaly in run 4 where v0.9 latency jumped; it corresponded to a background garbage collection on the host; Tom said you had some autoscaling events?
[05:56] Tom: yes there was a burst, autoscaler added a node but pod reattachment caused a KV cache cold start. that explains the spike.
[06:05] Priya: yeah that matches. warm pools and pre-warming can reduce that impact; we can recommend autoscale policies to keep a warm headroom.

[06:20] Maria: ok so decision time - do we pin v0.9 for canary? i'm leaning yes but need the replication on 2k and the prompt changes applied.
[06:31] Alex: proposal: start a 10% canary pinned to v0.9 with shadow sampling; run the 2k eval with prompt changes; set automatic gate: rollback to v1.0 if hallucination rate for the cohort exceeds 3.5% or increases >0.5% vs baseline; fallback to m-lite when cost per 1k tokens exceeds $X or Dedicated capacity drops below threshold.
[06:55] Maria: sounds reasonable. do we have pre-built dashboards for these cohorts?
[07:01] Daniel: yes we've added per-route dashboards in Redwood Console, can share link.

[07:12] Priya: also want to call out model compatibility for function/tool-calling — if you use structured tool outputs, make sure the pin is within same major model family to avoid schema drift.
[07:25] Evan: we do a lot of structured extraction for patient meds, so need to ensure the quantized model preserves the same parse.
[07:30] Priya: noted, we'll add that as a check in the gating suite.

[07:45] Alex: any blockers on infra side, Tom?
[07:48] Tom: just need the warm pool recommendations and maybe 2 extra GPUs for the dedicated canary window. budget approved for trial.
[07:56] Alex: great.

[08:05] Samantha: one more security item: SSO test. we need to validate SAML flow into Redwood Console. can we get a test tenant?
[08:13] Daniel: yes we can provision a test tenant; Alex will coordinate.

[08:22] Alex: ok recap of next steps — share model selection matrix and raw CSVs, Evan to run 2k eval with prompt changes, Priya to prep rollback runbook and canary gating steps, Samantha to confirm compliance doc list and SSO test. we'll reconvene next Tuesday same time unless urgent.
[08:44] Maria: thanks all.
[08:46] Group: bye.

Notes: transcript contains some auto-caption errors (KV cache was transcribed as KV cash in one segment), and speaker overlap labels may be approximate.
